title: Generalizing Hate Speech Detection Using Multi-Task Learning: A Case Study of Political Public Figures

bias_targets.methodology: Employing a leave-one-out cross-dataset evaluation scheme across nine hate speech datasets to measure how narrow, dataset-specific labeling criteria and definitions limit model generalization to unseen domains.

Using SHAP value analysis to identify top Islam-related keywords contributing to hate speech predictions, and calculating the Hopkins Statistic to measure the clustering tendency of Islamophobic content in the model's embedding space.
Calculating the Hopkins Statistic to evaluate the clustering distinctness of misogynistic posts in the model's embedding space and analyzing the frequency of gender-related keywords in tweets.
Analyzing the frequency of race-related keywords in tweets labeled as hateful and measuring the clustering tendency of these posts in the embedding space using the Hopkins Statistic.
Evaluating the distinctness of hate speech targeting immigrants and refugees by measuring its clustering tendency in the embedding space and identifying key predictive terms via SHAP analysis.
Comparing the volume and topics of hateful and abusive tweets generated by right-leaning versus left-leaning political figures, and analyzing political target terms.
